answer: Each identity bonds one shore segment with 70 credits. Per epoch its operator walks that segment, a wander transect, logging umber readings at five checkpoints with a beacon stamp. Auditors recompute turbidity bands from tide table and beacon log; out-of-band or unstamped readings burn the bond. Farther segments cost more: the kth filing costs 38+6(k-1) credits, the 1000th 6032, and 1000 fakes 3,035,000 plus 70,000 in bonds. A rented-walker ring fails: a walker cannot stamp two identities at one pulse; duplicates expose it. An honest agent walks one segment, pays one fee, recovers its bond.
